summary: Convert a raster data cube into a vector data cube
description:
Converts a raster data cube into a vector data cube by grouping connected pixels with the same value into polygons (also known as "polygonize").

Pixels are connected if they share an edge (pixels that only share a corner are not connected). Each connected area results in exactly one polygon, independent of how the implementation partitions the data. Areas with the same value that are not connected result in separate polygons. The polygons follow the pixel boundaries exactly (no smoothing or simplification) and may contain holes. The polygons are valid according to the OGC Simple Features specification, e.g. a hole that touches the exterior boundary at a single corner is an interior ring. No polygons are created for no-data values.

This process is meant for categorical data, e.g. land cover classes or masks. Continuous data should be quantized beforehand, e.g. with ``linear_scale_range()`` or ``round()``. Whether non-integer values are compared exactly or rounded is implementation-dependent.

The data cube must only contain the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`, as the polygons may differ for each label of other dimensions (e.g. for each date or band). Otherwise, a `TooManyDimensions` exception is thrown. Use processes such as ``filter_bands()``, ``reduce_dimension()`` or ``drop_dimension()`` to remove other dimensions beforehand.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A raster data cube with only the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`.

returns.description: A vector data cube with a single dimension of type `geometry`. The geometries are polygons in the spatial reference system of `data`, the values are the pixel values of the corresponding areas. The order of the geometries is not defined.

TooManyDimensions.message: The data cube must only contain the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`.
